Understanding how network traffic can be intercepted and modified is a cornerstone of cybersecurity—specifically for penetration testers and network administrators debugging secure connections. However, creating a script that is truly "undetected" is a complex task because modern networks employ various intrusion detection systems (IDS), encrypted protocols (TLS/SSL), and endpoint protection.
For educational and authorized testing purposes, here is a breakdown of how these systems work and the tools used to interact with them.1. The Core Concept: Man-in-the-Middle (MITM)To intercept traffic, you typically position yourself between two communicating parties. On a local network, this is often achieved through ARP Spoofing, where you tell a target device that your machine is the gateway, and tell the gateway that your machine is the target.2. Professional Tooling: MitmproxyFor intercepting and modifying web traffic (HTTP/HTTPS), mitmproxy is the industry standard.
